questions.question: With which of the following countries is the 'Navanna' festival associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Bengali harvest celebration is called Nabbana or** Navanna** and it is celebrated in Bangladesh, West Bengal, Tripura, and parts of Assam.
 
• The festival is celebrated with dance, music, and food.
 
• **Basant Panchmi** is the festival that marks the preparation for the arrival of the Spring season.
 
• **Pahela Falgun** is the first day of the Spring season according to the Bengali calendar whereas Pahela Baishakh is the first day of the Bengali calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harvest festival:**

 
 
• After three or four months of hard work there comes the day of the harvest.
 
• The sight of golden fields of standing crops, laden with grain, fills the hearts of farmers with joy and a sense of well-being.
 
• The efforts of the past season have borne fruit and it is time to relax and enjoy a little.
 
• The period of harvest is, thus, of great joy and happiness in all parts of India.
 
• Men and women celebrate it with great enthusiasm.
 
• Special festivals associated with the** harvest season** are **Pongal, Baisakhi, Holi, Diwali, Nabanya and Bihu.**

questions.question: In which of the following years was Bahadur Shah II deposed by the British and exiled to Rangoon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1857.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Bahadur Shah II (Bahadur Shah Zafar) was the last Mughal Emperor.

 
 
• **He was deposed by the British and exiled to Burma (Rangoon) following the Indian Rebellion of 1857.**
 
 
 
• The Revolt of 1857 had made a futile attempt to declare him the Emperor of India.
 
• He was captured by the English and sent to Rangoon where he died in 1862.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Revolt of 1857 began after the introduction of Enfield rifles enhanced the growing disaffection of sepoys.
 
• On 29th March 1857, a young sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry, Mangal Panday fired at the Sergeant Major in Barrackpore.
 
• Mangal Pandey and Ishwari Prasad were hanged and the whole regiment was disbanded. 
 
• This became the source of discontent among sepoys and the immediate cause of the revolt.

questions.question: In which of the years was the Reserve Bank of India nationalised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1949.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RBI was nationalized in 1949**.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised with effect from** 1st January 1949 **on the basis of the Reserve Bank of India (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.
 
• All shares in the capital of the Bank were deemed transferred to the Central Government on payment of suitable compensation.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the apex monetary Institution which controls Indian Rupee, monetary policy, and the banking system in India.
 
• The central bank was first established in the year 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. 
 
• After India's independence, the RBI was nationalized on 1 January 1949.
 
• RBI plays a vital role in the developmental strategy of the Government as it regulates the monetary policy of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

__
 
• The RBI Act empowers the Reserve Bank to perform Central Banking functions such as-
 
 
• Issue of currency notes.
 
• Government's banks.
 
• Banker of the commercial banks.
 
• Control of credit in the economy.
 
• The Reserve Bank has been given the power to issue licenses for open new banking companies and also for new branches.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is **India's central bank and regulatory body** and is responsible for the issue and supply of the Indian rupee and the regulation of the Indian banking system.

 
 
• **Governor:** Shaktikanta Das 
 
• **Founded: **1 April 1935, Kolkata
 
• **Headquarters:** Mumbai (Bombay), Maharashtra

questions.question: In which of the following sections of the Reorganisation act, 1966 is Chandigarh defined as a Union Territory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Section 4.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **In section 4 of the Reorganisation act, 1966 is Chandigarh defined as a Union Territory.**
 
• Chandigarh, which was made a Union Territory, served as the common capital of Punjab and Haryana.

 
• The Punjab Reorganisation Act was passed by the Indian Parliament on 18 September 1966, dissolving the former state of East Punjab.

 
 
• Based on the Shah Commission report in April 1966, the Punjab Reorganisation Act was passed by the Parliament.
 
 
 
• State Reorganisation Commission and Dass Commission made the recommendations that formed the basis for the Punjab Reorganisation Act, which created the states of Punjab and Haryana.
 
• Haryana became a part of the Punjab province. With the reorganization of Punjab on 1 November 1966, Haryana was made into a full-fledged State.
 
• Hilly Areas of Punjab were merged with Himachal Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Under Section 3:**

 
 
• It states that the "**Children and Adolescent Labor (Prohibition and Regulation) Act",** is a cognizable offence for a child of 14 years to work in any type of hazardous area or non-risk area.
 
 
 
• **Under Section 6:**
 
 
• It states that (Sexual Assault) of the POCSO Act, whoever commits a sexual assault shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a minimum term of 10 years.

questions.question: ______ are the oldest living tree species on Earth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bristlecone pines**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Bristlecone pines are the oldest non-clonal species on the planet.**
 
• These strange trees are** shaped by the wind, snow, and rain **has survived for thousands of years.
 
• Their ability to survive these harsh environments and adverse growing conditions is exactly their secret to great longevity.
 
• Bristlecone pines in** Great Basin National Park grow** in isolated groves just below the tree line. 
 
• The Great Basin Bristlecone Pines are an extremely rare species found only in **California, Nevada, and Utah.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Redwood **is a subfamily of coniferous trees within the family Cupressaceae.

 
 
• It includes the **largest and tallest trees** in the world.
 
• It is also known as **Sequoia sempervirens**.
 
• The native habitat of Redwood trees is only on the western slopes of the Sierra Nevada range of California.

questions.question: Which of the following Article of the Constitution of India deals with the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India?

• Article 151: Audit Reports.

• CAG has been given an independent position under the constitution of India, which is the instrument that ensures and promotes accountability of the executive to parliament.
 
• This office started functioning in 1858, and the first Auditor General was appointed in 1860.
 
• The CAG of India is an independent constitutional authority that is neither part of the legislature nor executive, though appointed by the President under his hand and seal and can be removed only through a motion of impeachment.
 
• Girish Chandra Murmu is the 14th and the current Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by fungus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ringworm.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ringworm **is caused by a type of fungus that eats keratin.
 
• The fungus that causes ringworm is called Microsporum.
 
• Ringworm is also known as dermatophytosis.
 
• Liverworts are a group of non-vascular plants similar to mosses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

__
 
• The body of the fungus is made up of filaments called** Mycelium.**
 
• A widely used antibiotic penicillin is produced from **Penicillium notatum.**
 
• Fungal diseases: Athlete foot, Ringworm, Candidiasis, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smallpox:**

 
 
• It is caused by the variola virus.
 
• It happens due to the change in weather conditions.
 
• Edward Jenner made the vaccine for Small Pox.
 
 
 
• **Polio:**
 
 
• Polio or Poliomyelitis is an infectious disease caused by the polio virus. Polio is transmitted through contaminated water or food, or contact with an infected person.
 
• Poliomyelitis, or simply Polio, is a highly contagious infectious disease caused by three types of Poliovirus.
 
• The Poliovirus is a virus that destroys the nervous system causing paralysis.
 
• Poliovirus is a highly contagious virus specific to humans.
 
• Jonas Salk discovered and developed the first polio vaccine.
 
• The first polio vaccine was the inactivated polio vaccine which came into use in 1955.

questions.question: A/an ______ is any substance that causes your immune system to produce antibodies against it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**the antigen.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The antigen **is a substance that stimulates the formation of antibodies and promotes the** immune system.**
 
• Antigens include toxins, chemicals, bacteria, viruses, or other substances that come from outside the body.
 
• Body tissues and cells, including cancer cells, also have antigens on them that can cause an immune response.
 
• In general, two main divisions of antigens are recognized:
 
 
• **Foreign antigens (or heteroantigens) **
 
• **Autoantigens (or self-antigens)​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protein:**

 
 
• It plays a role in many body processes:
 
• It supplies the body with energy.
 
• It helps in maintaining proper pH.
 
• They serve as hormones and messengers.
 
• Aids in biochemical reactions.
 
• Protein helps in growth and maintenance.
 
• It is helpful in immune system responses.
 
• It maintains proper fluid regulation and fluid balance.
 
 
 
• **Glucose:**
 
 
• It is the most abundant monosaccharide, a carbohydrate sub-category.
 
• During photosynthesis, glucose is primarily produced by plants and most algae from water and carbon dioxide, using energy from sunlight, where it is used to create the most abundant carbohydrate cellulose in cell walls.
 
• In the metabolism of energy, the most essential source of energy in all species is glucose.
 
• For metabolism, glucose is processed as a polymer, primarily as starch and amylopectin in plants, and as glycogen in animals. In the animals' blood, glucose circulates as blood sugar.
 
• In 1747, the German chemist Andreas Marggraf first isolated glucose from raisins.
 
 
 
• **Blood platelets**:
 
 
• Platelets are very large cell pieces in the bone marrow. Platelets are important for homeostasis because they aggregate to form platelet plugs that stop bleeding from small wounds. It is the source of Ca++ ions.
 
• **Life span:** 8-11 days.
 
• **Diameter:** 2-4 micrometre.
 
• **Normal platelets count:** 1.5 lakh - 4.5 lakh

__
 
• **The full form of OCD is Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.**
 
• Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a **mental and behavioural disorder **in which an individual has intrusive thoughts and feels the need to perform certain routines repeatedly to the extent where it induces distress or impairs general function.
 
• As indicated by the disorder's name, the primary symptoms of OCD are obsessions and compulsions.
 
• Obsessions are persistent unwanted thoughts,** mental images, or urges that generate feelings of anxiety, disgust, or discomfort.**
 
• Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is characterized by the occurrence of unwanted, intrusive obsessive thoughts and distressing images which are usually accompanied by compulsive behaviours. Compulsive behaviours are carried out either to undo or neutralize the obsessions or to prevent the occurrence of some dreadful event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anxiety disorders **are disorders that decrease the performance or social functioning of an individual due to hyper-anxiety.

 
 
• Anxiety disorder can be of many types such as generalized anxiety disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, somatoform disorder, etc.
 
 
 
• **Obsessive behaviour** is the inability to stop thinking about a particular idea or topic.
 
 
• The person involved, often finds these thoughts to be unpleasant and shameful.
 
 
 
• **Compulsive behaviour** is the need to perform certain behaviours over and over again.
 
 
• Many compulsions deal with counting, ordering, checking, touching, and washing.
 
• People affected by the obsessive-compulsive disorder are unable to control their preoccupation with specific ideas or are unable to prevent themselves from repeatedly carrying out a particular act or series of acts that affect their ability to carry out normal activities.

questions.question: Indian Universities Commission was set up in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1902.**__

• The Indian Universities Commission was appointed in 1902 by Lord Curzon to make recommendations for reforms in University education in India.
 
• Thomas Raleigh, Syed Hussain Belgrami, and, Gurdas Banerjee were its members.
 
• The Commission recommended regulations for the reformation of University Senates, greater representation of affiliated colleges in the senates, and stricter monitoring of them.
 
• It was responsible for passing the Indian Universities Act 1904.
 
• ** As per the University Act of 1904,**
 
 
• universities were to give more attention to study and research.
 
• the number of fellows of a university and their period in the office was reduced.
 
• five lakh rupees were to be sanctioned per annum for five years.
 
 
 
• Gokhale called it a **'retrograde measure'**.
 
• **Saddler University Commission came in 1917-19** to study the problems of Calcutta university.
 
• **Hartog Committee** came in 1929 for education reform.

questions.question: On which of the following dates is International Tiger Day observed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**29th July.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

Important Points__**

__
 
• International Tiger Day is observed on 29th July of every year.
 
• The day is also called Global Tiger Day.
 
• This day is celebrated every year to raise awareness for tiger conservation.
 
• The International Tiger Day was initially founded at the St. Petersburg Tiger Summit in 2010.__
 
• Over 97% of wild tigers had disappeared in the last century, with only around 3,000 left alive.
 
• International Tiger Day (also known as Global Tiger Day) is celebrated to promote the protection of the natural habitat of tigers and support tiger conservation issues.
 
• The annual day is celebrated with the slogan** "Their survival is in our hands".​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **According to WWF, only 3,890 tigers are left in the world, of them, India with more than 2500 tigers has the highest number**.
 
• It is an annual celebration to raise awareness regarding tiger conservation.
 
• It was instituted in 2010 at **Saint Petersberg Tiger Summit in Russia** in view of the alarming fall in the number of wild tigers.
 
• The summit had issued St. Petersburg Declaration on Tiger Conservation where Governments of tiger-populated countries had vowed to double the tiger population by the year 2020.

• It is the custodian of the records of the enduring value of the Government of India.

• It provides financial assistance to State/Union Territories.

• Private papers of eminent Indians.
 
• Microfilm copies of records of Indian interests from abroad.

questions.question: With which of the following states is the dance form 'Povadas associated'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Povadas dance** form is associated with **Maharashtra state.**
 
• Povadas are presented in the **Marathi ballad form.**
 
• This dance form describes the events in the life of the **great Maratha ruler, Shri Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.**
 
• The word Povada itself means** "the narration of a story in glorious terms".**
 
• The narratives are always odes in praise of an individual hero or an incident or place.
 
• The chief narrator is known as the **Shahir** who plays the duff to keep the rhythm.
 
• The tempo is fast and controlled by the main singer who is supported by others in the chorus.
 
• The earliest notable Powada was the** Afzal Khanacha Vadh (The Killing of Afzal Khan) (1659) by Agnidas which recorded Shivaji's encounter with Afzal Khan.**
 
• **Dhangari Gaja, Koli Dance, Lavani Dance, Povadas Dance, and Tamasha** are other dance forms of Maharashtra state. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dance forms of Karnataka:

 
 
• Kunitha, Yakshagana, Sannatas, Parijata, Doddatas, etc.
 
 

 
• Dance forms of Kerala:

 
 
• Theyyam, Thiruvathirakali, Chakyar Koothu Koodiyattam, Ottamthullal, Mohiniyattam, Kathakali, Padayani, etc. 
 
 
 
• Dance forms of Tamilnadu:
 
 
• Kumi, Kollatam, Mayil attam, Pulliyattam, Bharathnatyam etc.
